By using fully qualified syntax (<Type as Trait>::method), we explicitly specify which trait implementation to use, eliminating any ambiguity.

implementation_summary:
The fix addresses a subtle trait resolution conflict in Rust's type system that occurs when both TypedPath and OptionalFromRequestParts traits are implemented on the same type. The issue manifested as a compilation error where the wrong trait method was being invoked due to ambiguous trait resolution.

The solution uses fully qualified syntax (FQS) to explicitly specify which trait implementation should be used. Instead of calling `::axum::extract::Path::from_request_parts(parts, state)`, which relies on Rust's trait resolution rules, the fix generates `<::axum::extract::Path<#ident> as ::axum::extract::FromRequestParts<S>>::from_request_parts(parts, state)`. This explicitly states that we want the FromRequestParts trait implementation for Path<T>, eliminating any ambiguity with other traits that might have similarly named methods.

This change is minimal and surgical—it only affects the code generation in the typed_path macro and doesn't change any public APIs or behavior. The fix maintains backward compatibility while resolving the compilation error for users who encounter this specific trait conflict. The approach follows Rust best practices for disambiguating trait methods and ensures the framework remains robust in complex trait scenarios.
